comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose that the normalization of channel and customer inventory levels was a key driver impacting their segment revenues in fiscal year 2024, although with opposite directional effects on growth. NVDA's Graphics revenue grew 15% in Gaming specifically due to 'higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.' In contrast, AMD's Embedded segment revenue declined 33% because 'customers continued to normalize their inventory levels,' leading to lower demand. While both cite inventory normalization as a primary business driver, NVDA benefited from the resulting sell-in surge, whereas AMD experienced a revenue contraction due to pre-normalization destocking or continued reduced demand.

sentences.text: Graphics revenue - The year-on-year increase was led by growth in Gaming of 15% driven by higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.
Embedded net revenue of $3.6 billion in 2024 decreased by 33%, compared to net revenue of $5.3 billion in 2023.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.
